meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as an AI agent read them side by side. Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted; no mathematician has reviewed them.

topics.name: The SK model and Parisi functional
topics.description: The Hamiltonian, admissible order parameters, control value, diffusion and compact-strip regularity.

topics.name: Variational contact
topics.description: Feasible changes of coefficient or Stieltjes mass and the moment equalities they force on the support.

topics.name: Strict curvature on constant intervals
topics.description: Backward and forward shape estimates, the rational certificate and its integrated coercivity bound.

topics.name: Excluding support gaps
topics.description: The terminal, positive-height and zero-height gap arguments and their full-support conclusion.

topics.name: The scalar ground-state value
topics.description: The bounded martingale, terminal spin and the scalar identities and comparison bounds for the ground-state value.

topics.name: Finite Gaussian approximation
topics.description: Euler paths, curvature normalization, randomized rounding and convergence of the adjacent-correlation sum.

topics.name: Further consequences
topics.description: Consequences of the main argument with their own hypotheses and source scope.

topics.name: Formal statements and their scope
topics.description: The two formal models, their quantified endpoints and the distinctions needed to compare them with the paper.

notes.OAI.SKValue.Admissible: An admissible control starting at time $t$ is a process $\alpha$ that uses only the Brownian increments revealed since $t$ and satisfies $|\alpha_s(\omega)|\le1$. The definition combines `IsProgressive (shiftedFiltration W t) α` with a bound for every `s` and `ω`, rather than only almost everywhere. It is a predicate on an existing process. The support model instead bundles a control with proofs of these conditions; identifying the two representations requires a separate construction.
notes.OAI.SKValue.BrownianSpace: The probability space carrying the scalar model's Brownian motion. `W` bundles the sample type `Ω`, its `measurableSpace`, the measure `μ`, a proof `probability` that its total mass is one, and a real Brownian process `B`. The fields `measurable` and `brownian` provide its measurability and Brownian laws. The time argument of `B` is nonnegative real time. Unlike the support model's Brownian system, the sample type and measurable space are fields inside this object.
notes.OAI.SKValue.Certificate.integral_W_zero: The scalar certificate correction $W_2$ integrates to zero against the density $f$. The hypotheses supply the derivative chain $r'=v$, $v'=w$, $w'=z$, $s'=a$, $a'=d$, the density equation $f'=(r-s)f$, nonvanishing of $r$ away from zero, growth bounds and weighted integrability `hint`. Here the Lean parameter `a` is $s_x$, not the paper’s Hessian. This is the concrete correction identity in the scalar model, not a result for every polynomial $F$.
notes.OAI.SKValue.FiniteGaussianConclusion: The three conclusions promised for a fixed scalar-model cutoff $T$: eventual positivity of every active normalizer, convergence of the shifted correlation sum to $I(T)=\int_0^T\mathbb E[\Phi_{xx}(t,X_t)]\,dt$, and convergence of $I(S)$ to the ground-state value as $S\uparrow1$. In `∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ j < N`, one mesh threshold works for every active index of every later mesh. This proposition defines the outputs; it does not prove them. Its two limits are separate, with no rate or arbitrary joint limit.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion: An associated diffusion solves $X_t=B_t+\int_0^t\gamma(s)u(s,X_s)\,ds$ on $[0,1]$. The first conjunct makes the process stopped at time one adapted to `W.filtration`. The second places continuity and the equation for every time inside one `∀ᵐ ω` quantifier, so one probability-one event works throughout the interval. This scalar predicate uses real time and differs from the support model's globally progressive, nonnegative-time predicate. Equality of those versions is not part of this definition.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.L1_terminal: The diffusion position approaches its endpoint in mean absolute error: $\mathbb E|X_t-X_1|\to0$ as $t\uparrow1$. The only explicit premise is `hX : IsDiffusion W γ X`; no minimizing assumption or contact identity is needed. `𝓝[<] 1` means approach from below, and the integral is with respect to `W.μ`. This result permits the terminal position to pass through expectations when assembling the scalar value identity. Pathwise continuity comes separately from the diffusion predicate.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.contactPotential: The scalar contact potential has derivative $G'(s)=s-q(s)$ at every interior time. Here $q(s)=\mathbb E[u(s,X_s)^2]$, and $G(s)=\int_s^1(q(t)-t)\,dt$. The premises are `hX`, an associated diffusion, and `hs : s ∈ Ioo 0 1`, meaning $0<s<1$. `HasDerivAt` records an ordinary derivative at that point. This identifies the paper's $G'=-f$ when $f=q-t$ and turns vanishing contact potential into the moment identity.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.curvature_convex: The curvature second moment $t\mapsto\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]$ is convex on an interval where the scalar coefficient is constant. `hX` supplies the diffusion, `ha` and `hb` place the interval between zero and one, and `he` states $\gamma(t)=c$ for every $a<t<b$. The expression `jetMoment ... JetExpr.curvatureExpr` denotes this second moment. This is the non-strict convexity input used to exclude the positive-coefficient gap; it does not itself assert full support or a strict curvature bound.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.curvature_mean_i: The mean curvature is integrable over the entire time interval $[0,1]$. Besides `hX`, the theorem assumes strip regularity `hreg` and `ha`, the identity $\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]=1$ for $0\le t<1$. The proof bounds its absolute first moment by the square root of this second moment and combines that bound with measurability. `IntervalIntegrable ... volume 0 1` is integrability for the time integral. The declaration's conclusion is integrability; the Cauchy–Schwarz estimate occurs inside its proof.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.curvature_unit_m: The curvature second moment equals one at every time $0\le t<1$. The premises `hX` and `hreg` provide the associated scalar diffusion and regularity on each closed strip below one. The premise `hmom` is contact, $\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]=t$. The proof differentiates the integrated gradient-square identity using continuity of the curvature moment. Thus the unit curvature moment is derived from contact, rather than supplied as another minimizing assumption.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.finite_gaussian_: For a fixed $0<T<1$, all active normalizers eventually become positive and the shifted finite correlation sum converges to $\int_0^T\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)]\,dt$. Here `hT` and `hT1` fix the cutoff, `hg` supplies the gradient equation and strip bounds, `ha`, `huLip`, and `haLip` give curvature bounds and space-time Lipschitz estimates, and `hmom` gives unit curvature second moments. These are explicit premises of this helper. The conclusion contains neither the later $T\uparrow1$ limit nor a quantitative mesh threshold.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.groundState_eq_p: The scalar Parisi functional equals the limiting SK ground-state value whenever the supplied diffusion satisfies contact. The premise `hmom` states $\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]=t$ for all $0\le t<1$, alongside `hX : IsDiffusion W γ X`. Minimality is not an additional premise here: another theorem obtains contact from minimality. The proof combines the general Parisi upper comparison with finite Gaussian lower comparisons and their terminal limit. It provides an independent scalar-model route to the equality.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.moment_convexOn_: The gradient second moment $q(t)=\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]$ is convex wherever the scalar coefficient vanishes. `hX` supplies the diffusion, `ha` and `hb` keep the interval within $[0,1]$, and `he` asserts $\gamma(t)=0$ for every interior time. The conclusion is `ConvexOn ℝ (Ioo a b)`, so endpoints are excluded. Subtracting the affine function $t$ gives the paper's convexity of $f=q-t$. This handles the zero-coefficient case of the contact argument.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.parisi_first_val: The scalar Parisi functional is $\mathbb E|X_1|-\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dt$. The diffusion premise is `hX`; `hstrips` supplies the value and gradient equations and a space-time Lipschitz bound on every strip below one. The contact premise `hmoment` replaces the gradient second moment by $t$. This is a terminal expectation identity, before the functional has been identified with the SK ground-state value. It is one of the inputs assembled into the later three-formula value theorem.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.parisi_value_ass: A terminal spin $U$ realizes the scalar Parisi functional through the terminal position, the Brownian correlation, and the integrated mean curvature. The assumptions `hX`, `hreg`, `hmom`, and `hamom` supply the diffusion, strip regularity, contact, and unit curvature second moments. The conclusion also gives a stopped martingale, almost-sure and mean-square convergence to $U$, integrability of the curvature mean, and the cutoff integral's limit. These equalities concern `parisi W γ`; identifying it with `groundStateValue` is a further comparison theorem.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.strip_value_le_g: The cutoff integral $I(T)=\int_0^T\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)]\,dt$ does not exceed the SK ground-state value. The assumptions `hX` and `hmom` provide a scalar diffusion satisfying $q(t)=t$ on $[0,1)$, while `hT` and `hT1` require $0<T<1$. The proof passes the finite Gaussian lower comparison to the mesh limit. This theorem supplies the nonnegative side of the terminal loss. It does not state the bound $P_*-I(T)\le1-T$ or a covariance formula for that loss.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.terminal_gradien: The terminal gradient limit satisfies $UX_1=|X_1|$ almost surely. Besides `hX`, the premise `hd` requires differentiability of the scalar value function along the diffusion for times sufficiently near one, and `hU` gives the almost-sure limit of the gradient. At a nonzero endpoint the gradient tends to its sign; at a zero endpoint both products vanish. Consequently the conclusion does not require an atomlessness hypothesis for $X_1$. It supplies the product identity used in the terminal value assembly.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.terminal_product: The expected terminal product satisfies $\mathbb E[UX_1]=\mathbb E[UB_1]+\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dt$. Alongside `hX`, `hm` makes the gradient a unit-moment martingale, `hUm` makes $U$ measurable at time one, `hU` gives its bounded sampled limit, and `hc` gives path continuity before one. The factor $t$ already incorporates the contact second moment contained in `hm`. Thus this type is the contact-specialized version of the paper's earlier formula with $\gamma(t)\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]$.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsDiffusion.value_expectatio: At a cutoff $0<T<1$, the expected scalar value is its initial value plus $\tfrac12\int_0^T\gamma(t)\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]\,dt$. The assumptions `h` and `hg` supply the value and gradient strip equations; `hLu` and `huLip` give a nonnegative space-time Lipschitz bound, and `hX` supplies the diffusion. This formula precedes contact. Replacing the second moment by $t$ requires a separate contact identity; that replacement is not present in the theorem's hypotheses or conclusion.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsMinimizer: A scalar order parameter $\gamma$ minimizes the Parisi functional when `parisi W γ ≤ parisi W η` for every scalar `η : OrderParameter`. This definition quantifies over the entire admissible competitor type, with the Brownian space `W` fixed. It neither constructs a minimizer nor relates it to the support model's minimizer predicate. A transport argument must preserve functional values and cover every competitor, rather than identify the value at a single coefficient.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsMinimizer.coeff_constant_o: The minimizing scalar coefficient is constant inside any interval where the contact potential is strictly positive. The assumptions `hγ` and `hX` give minimality and its associated diffusion; `ha` and `hb` place the interval inside $[0,1]$. The premise `hG` requires $G(s)>0$ at every interior point. The conclusion compares $\gamma(s)$ and $\gamma(t)$ for every pair of interior times. It is the variational step that turns a hypothetical positive gap of $G$ into a constant-coefficient interval.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsMinimizer.contactPotential: The scalar contact potential is nonnegative at every $s\in[0,1]$. Here `hγ : IsMinimizer W γ` and `hX : IsDiffusion W γ X` are the substantive assumptions, and `hs` specifies the evaluation time. The potential integrates the excess second moment, $G(s)=\int_s^1(q(t)-t)\,dt$. Minimality supplies the variational inequality behind its sign. This is the starting inequality of the scalar contact route; vanishing of $G$ requires the later argument excluding positive gaps.

The scalar contact potential vanishes at every interior time of a minimizer. The premises are `hγ`, minimality of the scalar Parisi functional, `hX`, an associated diffusion, and `hx : x ∈ Ioo 0 1`. The proof assumes a positive gap, obtains constancy of the coefficient there, and rules out both positive- and zero-coefficient alternatives. This theorem addresses $0<x<1$; the ensuing moment theorem handles the time-zero endpoint separately.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsMinimizer.contact_origin_o: A minimizing scalar coefficient with $\gamma(0)>0$ has zero contact potential at the origin. The premise `hc` is this strict positivity, alongside minimality `hγ` and an associated diffusion `hX`. Removing a sufficiently small amount of initial mass gives the reverse variational inequality to the general nonnegativity result. The statement concerns $G(0)$, not directly $q(0)$. It supplies the left-endpoint condition for a positive-coefficient gap that begins at zero.
notes.OAI.SKValue.IsMinimizer.gradient_moment_: The gradient second moment equals time: $\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]=t$ for every $0\le t<1$. The only premises are a scalar minimizer `hγ` and its associated diffusion `hX`. The proof differentiates the vanishing contact potential in the interior and treats time zero separately. `Ico 0 1` includes zero and excludes one. This independent scalar route supplies contact without taking full Stieltjes support as a hypothesis, and then feeds the terminal and finite Gaussian results.
notes.OAI.SKValue.OrderParameter: The scalar order parameter is a real-time coefficient `coeff : ℝ → ℝ` with nonnegativity, monotonicity, and right continuity on $[0,1)$. Its `integrable` field requires integrability on $(0,1]$. The fields `nonneg`, `monotone`, and `rightContinuous` state those shape conditions explicitly; they do not impose the same conditions outside $[0,1)$. This real-time representation differs from the support model's half-open subtype. Endpoint and exterior values must therefore be handled when comparing the two models.
notes.OAI.SKValue.OrderParameter.origin_eq_of_: If an admissible scalar coefficient equals $c$ throughout $(0,b)$ with $b>0$, then its value at zero is also $c$. The premises are `hb : 0 < b` and `he`, the pointwise constancy on that interval. Right continuity is already a field of `γ : OrderParameter`, so it is not repeated as a premise. This small endpoint lemma lets a positive constant interval starting at zero invoke the origin contact theorem.
notes.OAI.SKValue.OrderParameter.zero: The identically zero function, bundled as an admissible scalar order parameter. Its `coeff` field is zero, and the other fields prove nonnegativity, monotonicity, right continuity, and integrability. There are no minimizing or diffusion hypotheses. This object is the coefficient used in the paper's heat examples. Defining it establishes admissibility only: the explicit heat formulas, the descent calculation, and the numerical lower bound require their own arguments.
notes.OAI.SKValue.ScalarValueConclusion: The promised scalar conclusion combines convergence of the finite-size ground-state sequence with a terminal spin $U$. The stopped gradient is a martingale, $U^2=1$ almost surely, and the gradient approaches $U$ both almost surely and in mean square. Three further conjuncts express the ground-state value using $|X_1|$, $UB_1$, and the mean curvature; the last conjunct states time integrability. This definition specifies outputs for `W`, `γ`, and `X`. It is not itself a theorem or an exact finite-time error estimate.
notes.OAI.SKValue.UnitMomentMartingale.exists_: A continuous unit-moment martingale has a terminal spin and remains a martingale after being held constant at that spin. The premise `h` includes boundedness by one and $\mathbb E[f_t^2]=t$; `hc` gives almost-sure continuity on $[0,1)$. The conclusion produces an `ℱ 1`-measurable $U$ with $U^2=1$, almost-sure convergence, and mean-square convergence. `𝓝[<] 1` means approach to one from below. This is a general martingale result, so an SK minimizer is not among its assumptions.
notes.OAI.SKValue.UnitMomentMartingale.termina: The earlier martingale value is the conditional expectation of its terminal limit: $\mathbb E[U\mid\mathcal F_s]=f_s$ for $0\le s<1$. The premise `h` is the unit-moment martingale structure, `hUm` makes $U$ measurable at time one, and `hU` supplies a bounded almost-sure limit along `terminalTime n`. The notation `=ᵐ[μ]` means equality almost everywhere. This projection identity is the input for the paper's exact mean-square calculation, rather than a statement of that calculation itself.

The mean-square error $\mathbb E[(f_t-U)^2]$ tends to zero as $t\uparrow1$. A point outside the support, with some support point to its right, yields endpoints $0\le a<b<1$ such that $b$ is in the support, the interior is support-free, and either $a=0$ or $a$ is in the support. If no terminal constant interval is possible, then every `x : Time` has a larger point in the Stieltjes support. The hypotheses `hγ` and `hμ` connect the coefficient and measure, while `hend` excludes every nonnegative terminal plateau. This supplies a finite right support point for the gap analysis. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Time: The type of overlap times $t$ with $0\le t<1$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.exists_fee: For every $\varepsilon>0$, the lemma constructs a progressively measurable control bounded by one whose payoff is at least $F(0,x)-\varepsilon$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.expected_v: One time step of a controlled Brownian path satisfies an expected value-minus-cost upper bound, with explicit discretization errors. The remainder contains terms of orders $h^{3/2}$ and $h^2$. This is a finite-step inequality used to justify verification; it is not itself the continuous Itô drift identity.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.abs_le_value: The control value satisfies $|x|\le\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$ for every admissible coefficient and `ht : t≤1`. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actualQuartic_pos: At every positive time, $\mathbb E[\Phi_{xx}(t,X_t)^4]>0$ for every admissible coefficient. It does not need a plateau or prove that the Hessian is positive at every point. With $v=c\Phi_{xx}$ and $c>0$, it gives the paper’s scaled positivity.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actualThirdSquare_: At every positive time, $\mathbb E[\Phi_{xxx}(t,X_t)^2]>0$ for any admissible coefficient. The condition `ht : 0 < (t : ℝ)` excludes the initial deterministic point. The proof combines a nonzero third derivative somewhere with positive probability on an open neighborhood and continuity of the derivative. On a zero plateau this moment is $q''$, but the positivity theorem itself is not restricted to zero coefficients.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actual_coercivity: At a positive time where the order parameter is continuous, the limiting diffusion satisfies the scaled coercive inequality. The explicit hypotheses are `ht0 : 0 < (t : ℝ)` and `ht : ContinuousAt γ.val t`; `t : Time` already means $0\le t<1$. The theorem does not assume minimality or a plateau. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.approxError_limit: The error of the designated coefficient-and-terminal approximation tends to zero. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.approxValue_deriva: Every fixed spatial derivative of `approxValue γ n` converges uniformly to the corresponding derivative of $\Phi_\gamma$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.approxValue_error: The designated finite-step value differs from the control-defined value by at most `approxError γ n`, uniformly for $0\le t\le1$ and every $x$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.compactJetField_ge: The generator applied to the spatial curvature $a=\Phi_{xx}$ is $-\gamma a^2$ on a fixed strip. The generator applied to $b=\Phi_{xxx}$ is $-3\gamma ab$ on a compact strip. The hypotheses only require an admissible coefficient and $0\le T<1$. Here `compactJet ... 1` is $a=\Phi_{xx}$ and `compactJet ... 2` is $b$. For a constant coefficient $c$, multiplication by $c$ gives the drift $-3vw$ of $w=cb$, with $v=ca$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.compactMixedDrift: The drift $\beta(\widetilde u+u)/2$ used when comparing the values for coefficients $\beta$ and $\gamma$, with time truncated to a fixed strip. Here $\widetilde u=\Phi_{\beta,x}$ and $u=\Phi_{\gamma,x}$; the coefficient `β` multiplies their average. This choice cancels the first-order spatial term in the difference equation. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.compactMixedDrift_: On a fixed strip ending at $T<1$, the absolute value of the comparison drift is at most $\beta(T)$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.compactMixedGradie: The arithmetic mean $(\Phi_{\beta,x}+\Phi_{\gamma,x})/2$, with both gradients evaluated using the same time cutoff `T`. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.contactPotential: The tail integral $G(s)=\int_s^1(q(t)-t)\,dt$ for the canonical diffusion associated with `W` and `γ`. The integrand compares the squared-gradient moment with the overlap time. This declaration defines the potential for any admissible coefficient. Its nonnegativity and vanishing on Stieltjes support require minimality and are proved separately; they are not built into the definition.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.contactPotential_c: For a minimizer, the contact potential has nonpositive integral over every compact subset of its Stieltjes measure. The assumptions are `hmin`, the cumulative-measure relation `hμ`, and `hK : IsCompact K`. Local finiteness makes the restricted measure finite, so its mass can be removed through an admissible competitor. Combined with $G\ge0$, this gives zero compact integrals and hence contact on the entire relative support.

The contact potential is continuous on the closed interval $[0,1]$ for every admissible coefficient. Lean states this as `ContinuousOn (contactPotential W γ) (Icc 0 1)`. The proof uses integrability of $q(t)-t$ and continuity of an integral with moving lower endpoint. No minimality is assumed. This is the continuity that turns the integral contact inequalities into pointwise vanishing on support.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.contactPotential_h: At every interior time $0<s<1$, $G'(s)=s-q(s)$. The condition `hs : s∈Ioo 0 1` is explicit. The proof differentiates the moving lower endpoint of the tail integral, using continuity of the squared-gradient moment. This declaration supplies an ordinary two-sided derivative only in the interior; the endpoint slope argument at zero needs its own one-sided reasoning.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.contactPotential_n: For a minimizing coefficient, $G(s)\ge0$ at every overlap time $s<1$, including zero. The hypothesis is `hmin : IsMinimizer W γ`, and `s : Time` already records $0\le s<1$. The proof adds a Dirac mass at $s$ to the Stieltjes measure and applies the variational inequality. Because total mass is unconstrained, this competitor needs no compensating removal elsewhere.

For a minimizer, $\int G\,d
u\le0$ for every finite submeasure $
u\le\mu_\gamma$. The assumptions `hμ`, `hν` and `[IsFiniteMeasure ν]` identify the cumulative measure and the removable part. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff: The random payoff of an admissible control: the absolute terminal state minus one half of the integrated cost $\gamma\alpha^2$. The state starts from `x` at time `t`, accumulates Brownian increments and the drift $\int_t^1\gamma\alpha$. The argument `α : Control W (Real.toNNReal t)` carries progressive measurability and the bound one. This is a pathwise payoff; the value takes its expectation and then the supremum over controls.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff_coef: Using the same control under two admissible coefficients changes its payoff by at most three halves of their $L^1$ distance over the remaining interval. The theorem is a one-sided pathwise inequality for each sample `ω`; swapping `γ` and `η` gives the other direction. The terminal absolute value contributes one copy of the distance and the quadratic cost contributes one half. The assumption `ht : t≤1` fixes the interval orientation.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff_le: Every admissible control has payoff at most $|x+B_1-B_t|+\frac12\int_t^1\gamma(s)\,ds$. The assumptions are only admissibility and `ht : t≤1`. After expectation, this becomes the upper half of the terminal estimate without differentiating the absolute-value terminal datum.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvature: The spatial curvature $a(t,x)=\Phi_{\gamma,xx}(t,x)$, defined as the derivative of `gradient W γ t`. The term curvature here concerns the variable $x$; it is distinct from time curvature of the moment $q(t)$. Lean's `deriv` is a total operator, so differentiability and sign properties are not supplied by this definition. They are established by the compact-strip regularity and convexity results.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_co: The function $t\mapsto\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]$ is continuous on every fixed strip $[0,T]$ with $T<1$. The assumptions `hT0` and `hT1` specify that strip. Combining this continuity with the derivative identity for $q$ gives continuous differentiability of $q$ below terminal time, including its right derivative at zero.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_de: On an open interval where the coefficient equals a constant $c$, the derivative of the curvature moment has derivative `stripThird`. The condition `hc` asserts constancy throughout that interval; `ht` places the time inside it, and `hbT` keeps it below a compact-strip cutoff $T<1$. Since the curvature moment is $q'$, this is the plateau identity for $q'''$. It does not establish the formula containing $\gamma'$ for a varying smooth coefficient.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_ha: On an open interval where $\gamma=c$, the derivative of the curvature moment is `stripSecond`. The hypothesis `hc` gives constancy, `ht` requires an interior time, and `hbT` bounds the interval by a compact-strip cutoff $T<1$. Since the curvature moment is $q'$, setting $c=0$ identifies $q''$ with the square moment of the third spatial derivative. No time derivative at a coefficient jump is asserted.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvature_nonneg: The spatial curvature $\Phi_{\gamma,xx}(t,x)$ is nonnegative for every admissible coefficient, every $0\le t<1$ and every $x$. The time assumptions are `ht0` and `ht1`. Convexity makes the spatial gradient nondecreasing, and differentiation gives the sign. This is a pointwise spatial statement; it does not assert positivity of a time derivative of $q$, nor does it require a minimizing coefficient.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.differenceField: The field $D=\Phi_\beta-\Phi_\gamma$ on a fixed compact time strip, bundled with the regularity needed for the expectation identities. The assumptions `hT0 : 0≤T` and `hT1 : T<1` keep the field away from terminal time. Its spatial value and time rate are defined by subtracting the corresponding fields for the two coefficients. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.differenceField_ge: Write $\widetilde u=\Phi_{\beta,x}$ and $u=\Phi_{\gamma,x}$. Under the comparison drift $\beta(\widetilde u+u)/2$, the generator of $D=\Phi_\beta-\Phi_\gamma$ equals $-\frac12(\beta-\gamma)u^2$. The compact-strip hypotheses are `hT0` and `hT1`. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_interval: At every positive time, the associated diffusion assigns positive probability to every nonempty open spatial interval. The hypotheses are `ht : 0 < (t : ℝ)` and `hab : a < b`; no plateau or minimizing assumption is needed. This supplies enough support to turn a continuous nonzero derivative into a positive even moment. The statement does not itself assert that a probability density exists or is positive at every point.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_isDiffus: The constructed process `diffusion W γ` satisfies the full associated-diffusion predicate for every admissible coefficient. Its conclusion includes progressivity, almost sure continuity through time one, the zero initial condition and the integral feedback equation. The inputs are only the Brownian system `W` and `γ`; minimality is unnecessary. Subsequent moment calculations can therefore use this canonical process before any variational assumptions are introduced.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_uniquene: Every associated diffusion equals the constructed diffusion almost surely, simultaneously for all times through one. The assumption `hX : IsDiffusion W γ X` says it solves the required diffusion equation with the given Brownian system and coefficient. The conclusion’s single almost-sure set precedes the quantifier over time. This permits transferring the moment identities from the constructed diffusion to any associated one; it does not enlarge the time domain of the value-function theorem.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.eulerNormalizer: The normalizer $c_j$ is the reciprocal square root of the support-model Euler curvature second moment. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.finiteCDF_fubini: For a finite measure $\nu$ on $[0,1)$ and an integrable function $H$, integrating its cumulative mass against $H(t)$ equals integrating the tail $\int_s^1H(t)\,dt$ against $\nu(ds)$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.finiteValue_contro: A regular finite-step problem approximates the absolute-value-terminal control value with error at most the terminal uniform error plus three halves of the coefficient $L^1$ error. The mesh spans exactly one by `hN : N*h=1`; `hf` and `hLip` give terminal regularity and the one-Lipschitz bound, and `he` bounds its difference from $|x|$. This comparison has one finite-step side and one control-value side, not two arbitrary smooth-terminal problems.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.full_support: Every supplied minimizing coefficient has full relative Stieltjes support on $[0,1)$ and is strictly increasing. For every associated diffusion $X$, the moments satisfy $\mathbb E[\Phi_x(t,X_t)^2]=t$ and $\mathbb E[\Phi_{xx}(t,X_t)^2]=1$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gaussianCoeffA: The support-model coefficient $A_j$ pairs the randomized terminal sign with the normalized curvature increment $g_j$. This definition specifies the first coefficient vector exactly but proves neither orthonormality of the increment family nor its asymptotic relation to the curvature mean.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gaussianCoeffB: The support-model coefficient $B_i$ is the expectation of the randomized terminal sign times Gaussian coordinate $Z_i$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient: The spatial gradient $u(t,x)=\Phi_{\gamma,x}(t,x)$. Lean writes it as `deriv (value W γ t) x`, differentiating in space with the time and coefficient held fixed. This declaration only defines the notation. The gradient's bound by one, its zero-field symmetry and its martingale behavior along the associated diffusion are separate statements, used at different stages of the support and scalar-value arguments.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient_zero: For every admissible coefficient and $0\le t<1$, the spatial gradient at $x=0$ vanishes. The time assumptions are `ht0` and `ht1`. Evenness of the zero-field value makes its gradient odd, hence zero at the origin. In particular $u(0,0)=0$, which supplies the initial condition for the squared-gradient moment; it is not inferred from a one-sided minimum of the contact potential.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.incrementFiltratio: The natural filtration of the increment process $B_{t+s}-B_t$, indexed by elapsed time $s\ge0$. At elapsed time $s$, this filtration records the increments observed between the starting time $t$ and the current time $t+s$. Controls starting at $t$ must be progressively measurable for it. The time index is relative to its start; the information available at each observation ends at the control's current time.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.minimizer_contact: At each support point of a minimizing coefficient’s Stieltjes measure, the squared-gradient moment equals time and the curvature moment is at most one. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.minimizer_full_sup: For a minimizing coefficient and a supplied Stieltjes measure, the measure has full support, the coefficient is strictly increasing, and both moment identities hold along the constructed diffusion. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.minimizer_no_termi: A minimizing coefficient cannot be constant on any interval $(a,1)$ with $0\le a<1$ and finite height $c\ge0$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.minimizer_variatio: For a minimizer $\gamma$ and every admissible competitor $\beta$, the integral $\int_0^1(\beta-\gamma)(q(t)-t)\,dt$ is nonnegative. The hypotheses are `hmin` and the typed competitor `β : OrderParameter`. The proof uses the limit along the prescribed chord sequence and nonnegativity of each difference quotient. This is the variational inequality needed for mass addition and removal; it does not itself declare a full real right derivative in arbitrary directions.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixedPath_error: The comparison path for coefficients $\beta,\gamma$ stays close to the canonical $\gamma$ diffusion when their coefficient $L^1$ distance and gradient difference are small. The bound is $2(\|\beta-\gamma\|_1+\gamma(T)T\delta)e^{LT}$ with the stored drift rate $L$. It is pathwise in `ξ`, for the common Brownian driving path.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixedQ: The expected square of $\Phi_{\gamma,x}$ evaluated along the comparison diffusion built from $\beta$ and $\gamma$, on the cutoff strip `T`. The gradient belongs to the original coefficient, while the path uses the average-gradient comparison drift. This distinction is what makes the exact finite-change formula work. Setting the perturbed coefficient close to $\gamma$ later turns this mixed expectation into the ordinary moment $q$.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixedQ_perturbatio: For a fixed cutoff and observation time, the mixed squared-gradient moments tend to the canonical moment of $\gamma$ as the prescribed chord perturbations approach $\gamma$. The statement is convergence along that sequence, rather than a limit over every positive real perturbation parameter.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixedQ_weighted_li: The integrals of the mixed moments, weighted by the coefficient direction $\beta-\gamma$, converge on a fixed interval $[0,T]$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixedStripDrift: The comparison drift bundled as a bounded spatially Lipschitz function. Its value is the truncated $\beta$ coefficient times the average of the two truncated gradients. The bound is $\beta(T)$, while the Lipschitz constant is chosen from the compact-strip gradient estimates. The cutoff `T : Time` guarantees $T<1$. This bundle lets the diffusion construction act on the comparison equation used in the first-variation proof.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixed_difference_i: The value difference at $(0,0)$ equals its expected difference at the cutoff $T$, plus one half of the integral of $(\beta-\gamma)$ times the mixed squared-gradient moment. Both coefficients are admissible, and `T : Time` stays below one. The terminal expectation is retained exactly. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.mixed_difference_t: The absolute expected value difference at cutoff $T$ is at most $\frac32\int_T^1|\beta-\gamma|$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.normalizedIncremen: The support-model increment $g_j=c_j a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})Z_j$. The definition multiplies `eulerNormalizer` by the curvature at the previous Euler point and Gaussian coordinate `j-1`. Its paper index is therefore one-based, with active range $1\le j\le N$. The final coordinate $Z_{N+1}$ is reserved for rounding and is not an increment of this family. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.normalizedParisiDi: The normalized Parisi-functional difference along the prescribed chord equals the normalized value difference minus $\frac12\int_0^1t(\beta-\gamma)(t)\,dt$. Isolating the linear penalty leaves the convergence argument to act only on the nonlinear value term.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.normalizedValueDif: The normalized value quotient along the prescribed chord differs from its mixed-moment integral over $[0,T]$ by at most $\frac32\int_T^1|\beta-\gamma|$. The inputs `T` and `n` remain independent, so the bound is uniform in the chord index. It justifies controlling terminal tails before taking the chord limit. Its statement still concerns the discrete perturbations with step $1/(n+1)$, not every real positive step.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parameterMeasure_i: The canonical measure `parameterMeasure γ` has cumulative mass $\mu([0,t])=\gamma(t)$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parisi: The functional $\mathcal P(\gamma)=\Phi_\gamma(0,0)-\frac12\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dt$. The first term is the stochastic control value, and the second is the deterministic Parisi penalty in the normalization $\xi''=1$. Lean uses the coefficient's zero extension in the integral. This definition does not identify the functional with an SK ground-state energy; that equality is a separate theorem for a minimizing coefficient.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parisi_chord_deriv: For admissible endpoints $\gamma,\beta$, the difference quotients along $\gamma_n=(1-\varepsilon_n)\gamma+\varepsilon_n\beta$, with $\varepsilon_n=1/(n+1)$, converge to $\frac12\int_0^1(\beta-\gamma)(q-t)\,dt$, where $q(t)=\mathbb E[\Phi_x(t,X_t)^2]$ along the constructed diffusion. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.perturbation_dista: The $L^1$ coefficient distance between `perturbation γ β n` and $\gamma$ tends to zero. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveCoeff_boun: Each coefficient in the designated positive-step approximation is at most `positiveTerminal γ n`. The latter combines the growing term $n+1$ with the largest sampled coefficient, so it can serve as the log-cosh smoothing parameter. The bound holds for every step index `j`. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positivePath_error: The canonical diffusion and the designated positive-step feedback path differ by at most $2(E_n+\gamma(T)T\delta)e^{LT}$ up to cutoff $T$. Here $E_n$ is `positiveCoeffError γ n`, `hd` bounds the gradient error by $\delta\ge0$, and $L$ is the stored canonical drift rate. The bound is deterministic for each sample path `ξ`. Its constant and coefficient factor differ from the sharper illustrative estimate printed in the paper.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveValue_deri: For each fixed spatial derivative order, the designated positive-step values converge uniformly to the control value on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$, with $T<1$. The conditions `hT0` and `hT1` delimit the strip. These approximants use their specified coefficient sampling, positive offset and terminal smoothing. The theorem is useful for the coercivity limit, but it does not quantify over arbitrary smooth-terminal approximation sequences.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positive_gap_curva: If an admissible coefficient equals $c>0$ on $(a,b)$ with $0\le a<b<1$, then the second derivative of the curvature moment is positive throughout that interval. The hypotheses `ha`, `hab`, `hb`, `hc0` and `hc` spell out this domain and plateau. Since the curvature moment is $q'$, this gives $q'''>0$. The theorem assumes no minimizer and makes no assertion at the plateau endpoints or at coefficient jumps.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.quarticMoment_scal: The fourth moment expression for the derivative of $r=c f'$ is $c^4(f'')^4$. The hypothesis `hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f` permits differentiating the scaled gradient, and the identity holds for every real `c` and spatial point `x`. This is the left-hand rescaling used alongside the curvature polynomial. It explains why division of the full inequality by $c^2$ leaves a factor $c^2$ in front of the unscaled fourth moment.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.randomizedSign: The support-model terminal sign is $\operatorname{sign}(u(T,Y_N)+2\Phi_{\rm N}(Z_{N+1})-1)$, where $\Phi_{\rm N}$ is the standard-normal distribution function and $Z_{N+1}$ is the extra independent coordinate. The source casts `SignType.sign` to a real number and uses `gaussianCoordinate N N` for the extra coordinate. The Euler endpoint has already been formed from the first $N$ coordinates. This definition fixes the random variable only. Showing that its mean preserves the endpoint gradient, and that its zero event is null, requires separate integration arguments.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.sampleCoercive_int: The expectations of the sampled coercive polynomial converge to the polynomial formed from the limiting second, third and fourth spatial derivatives. The hypothesis `ht : ContinuousAt γ.val t` ensures convergence of the sampled coefficient as well as the derivatives. The proof uses common bounds and dominated convergence. Its formal approximation uses a uniform grid and left sample times; the conclusion does not quantify over arbitrary approximating sequences or state the paper’s explicit error constants.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.sampleJet_limit: The sampled derivative of any order converges almost surely to that derivative of the value function evaluated along the limiting diffusion. The parameters are `W`, `γ`, `t` and the derivative order `m`; there is no continuity assumption on the coefficient at $t$ in this lemma. The approximation is evaluated at `sampleTime n t` and along `positivePath`. This differs from the paper’s illustrative construction with an exact frozen plateau centered at $t$.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.sampleQuartic_inte: The sampled fourth-moment polynomial converges in expectation to $\gamma(t)^4\mathbb E[\Phi_{xx}(t,X_t)^4]$. The hypothesis `ht : ContinuousAt γ.val t` supplies convergence of the coefficient sampled from the left. A uniform bound on the sampled second derivative gives domination. This result is the left-hand limit in the coercivity argument; it does not require convergence of the auxiliary forward scores or their quotient variables.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment: The scalar function $q(t)=\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]$ for a supplied process `X`. The expectation is taken under the Brownian system's law, and `gradient W γ` is the spatial derivative of the control value. This declaration is meaningful before one assumes that `X` is an associated diffusion or that $\gamma$ minimizes the functional. Derivative identities and the later equality $q(t)=t$ are separate results.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_bound: Along the canonical diffusion, the squared-gradient moment is nonnegative and at most one for every `t≤1`. Lean states nonnegativity together with the absolute-value bound $|q(t)|\le1$, which is equivalent to the usual upper bound once nonnegativity is known. The result uses the bound $|u|\le1$ and the probability law. No minimization or contact assumption is needed.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_eq_in: For $0\le t<1$, the canonical squared-gradient moment equals $\int_0^t\mathbb E[a(s,X_s)^2]\,ds$. The conditions are `ht0` and `ht1`; admissibility is built into `γ`. This is the moment-level identity following from the gradient martingale and the zero initial gradient. Its conclusion does not itself state a pathwise stochastic-integral representation of $u(t,X_t)$.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_hasDe: The derivative of $q$ within the nonnegative-time half-line is the curvature second moment for every $0\le t<1$. Lean writes this as `HasDerivWithinAt ... (Ici 0) t`. At an interior positive time it agrees with the ordinary derivative, and at zero it gives the right derivative. This holds for every admissible coefficient along the canonical diffusion, before minimality is imposed.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_zero: The squared-gradient moment of the constructed diffusion is zero at time zero: $q(0)=0$. The parameters are the Brownian system `W` and any admissible order parameter `γ`; no minimizing or support hypothesis is required. The proof uses the integrated moment identity with identical integration endpoints. This supplies the initial value needed in the zero-gap contradiction. The theorem states that value directly rather than merely accepting it as a premise called `hq0`.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripA_hasDerivAt_: Inside an interval where the truncated coefficient equals $c$, the strip curvature second moment has derivative `stripSecond`. The assumptions `hc` and `ht` express constancy and interior membership, and `hbT` places the interval within the cutoff. This is a local time statement. The corresponding theorem for the untruncated canonical moment follows by identifying the two processes and their derivative fields on the strip.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripSecond_eq_act: The compact-strip second-moment expression is $\mathbb E[b^2-2ca^3]$, with $a=\Phi_{xx}$ and $b=\Phi_{xxx}$ evaluated along the diffusion. The hypothesis `htT : t ≤ T` places the time inside the compact strip, while `c` is any real constant. At $c=0$ only the nonnegative square remains. The declaration identifies the polynomial; the separate plateau derivative theorem identifies it with $q''$.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripSecond_hasDer: On an open interval where the truncated coefficient is constant with value $c$, the derivative of `stripSecond` is `stripThird`. The assumptions `hc`, `ht` and `hbT` express that local setting. This supplies the next step in the chain from $q'$ to $q'''$. The statement does not pass a third time derivative through an approximation limit or differentiate the coefficient at a jump.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_coerciv: The third-moment expression obeys $c^2\mathrm{stripThird}\ge c^4\mathbb E a^4/1000$, with $c=\gamma(t)$. The conditions `ht`, `htT` and `hcont` require positive time, inclusion in the chosen compact strip and continuity of the coefficient at that time. This scaled form remains meaningful at $c=0$. notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_eq_actu: The compact-strip third-moment expression equals $\mathbb E[d^2-12cab^2+6c^2a^4]$, where $a,b,d$ are the second, third and fourth derivatives of the value function along the diffusion. Calling it $q'''$ additionally requires a derivative theorem on a constant-coefficient interval.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_pos: The third-moment expression is strictly positive at a positive continuity point where $\gamma(t)>0$. The explicit conditions are `ht`, `htT`, `hcont` and `hc`. The proof combines the scaled coercive bound with strict positivity of the fourth curvature moment and then removes the positive factor $\gamma(t)^2$. This is a spatial-moment conclusion; a plateau derivative identity is what turns it into strict curvature of $q'$.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.terminal_plateau_s: On a terminal plateau of nonnegative finite height $c$, the deficit $1-q(T)$ is at least $C\sqrt{1-T}$ for some $C>0$ near one. The assumptions include plateau constancy `hc`, a positive reference time `s`, and `a<s<1`. The conclusion specifies $T\ge(s+1)/2$ and $8\,\mathrm{kernelConstant}\,c\sqrt{1-T}\le1/2$. It requires no minimizer. The formal proof uses bounded smooth tests and a small window, rather than the paper’s particular pointwise density constants.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.terminal_plateau_t: Within a terminal plateau, the expectation of a bounded smooth test function at time `T` equals its tilted Gaussian transition evaluated at the diffusion at time `s`. The conditions `hc0` and `hc` give the nonnegative constant height, while `has` and `hsT` place the two times in the plateau. The test hypothesis is `hg : BoundedSmooth g`. This is an expectation identity; it does not directly state a pointwise density kernel.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.third_not_identica: At each $0\le t<1$, the spatial derivative of the curvature is nonzero somewhere. The hypotheses `ht0` and `ht1` specify this time range; there is no plateau or minimizing condition. If it vanished everywhere, the gradient and value would be forced into polynomial forms incompatible with the value’s behavior relative to $|x|$. The conclusion is existential in the spatial variable, not a claim that the third derivative is nonzero everywhere.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value: The value $\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$ is the supremum, over admissible controls, of the expected terminal absolute value minus the quadratic control cost. In Lean, `sSup (Set.range ...)` takes that supremum over the type `Control W (Real.toNNReal t)`, so progressivity and the bound one are part of the allowed control. This definition selects the solution subsequently shown to satisfy the PDE; it does not define the value by the PDE alone.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.valueRate: The expression $-\frac12\Phi_{xx}-\frac12\gamma\Phi_x^2$ appearing in the time equation for the value. It is defined from `curvature`, `gradient` and the coefficient's zero extension. This declaration names the rate without asserting differentiability in time. The integral-rate theorem and the right-derivative theorem separately relate it to the time dependence of the control-defined value on compact strips.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_coefficient_: Changing the admissible coefficient from $\gamma$ to $\eta$ changes the value at $(t,x)$ by at most $\frac32\int_t^1|\gamma-\eta|$. The terminal datum is $|x|$ on both sides, and `ht : t≤1` fixes the time interval. The bound is uniform in the spatial variable. It follows by comparing the payoff of the same admissible control, then taking suprema in both directions.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_derivative_c: Every fixed spatial derivative of the value is jointly continuous in time and space on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$ when $T<1$. The derivative order `m` may be zero, in which case the result is continuity of the value itself. The assumptions `hT0` and `hT1` delimit the compact time strip. This is continuity of spatial derivatives, not an assertion that all time derivatives remain continuous across coefficient jumps.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_derivative_h: At each $0\le t<T<1$, every spatial derivative of the value has a right time derivative given by the corresponding spatial derivative of the compact value rate. The assumptions are `hT0`, `hT1`, `ht0` and `htT`. Lean's `HasDerivWithinAt ... (Ioi t) t` specifically approaches time $t$ from the right. It is not the same formal statement as an almost-everywhere two-sided time derivative.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_derivative_t: For a fixed derivative order and cutoff $T<1$, one constant bounds the time change of that spatial derivative by $C|b-a|$, uniformly over $a,b\in[0,T]$ and every $x$. The hypotheses are `hT0` and `hT1`. Thus each such derivative is locally absolutely continuous in time. The statement controls time increments even when the coefficient jumps, without requiring a classical time derivative at every point.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_even: The value is even in its spatial argument for every admissible coefficient and $0\le t\le1$. These time restrictions are `ht0` and `ht1`. Reflection symmetry of the Brownian control problem and the absolute-value terminal reward give $\Phi_\gamma(t,-x)=\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$. Differentiating this identity below terminal time makes the gradient odd and forces its value at the spatial origin to be zero.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_integral_rat: The change in value between times $a$ and $b$ equals the integral of `valueRate` over that interval. The assumptions are `ha : 0≤a`, `hab : a≤b` and `hb : b<1`, with the spatial point `x` fixed. This formulation expresses the time equation without demanding classical differentiation across coefficient jumps. Together with absolute continuity, it yields the PDE almost everywhere on compact time strips.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_on_terminal_: On a terminal plateau $\gamma=c\ge0$, the value at time $t<1$ is the logarithmic Gaussian evolution of $|x|$ over variance $1-t$. The conditions `hc0`, `ht0`, `hat`, `ht1` and `hc` specify the height, time and plateau. For $c>0$ this is $c^{-1}\log\mathbb E e^{c|x+\sqrt{1-t}Z|}$; the formal `varianceLogHeat` also has the ordinary heat interpretation at $c=0$.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_terminal_uni: For $0\le t\le1$, the value lies between $|x|$ and $|x|+\sqrt{2(1-t)/\pi}+\frac12\int_t^1\gamma(s)\,ds$. The conditions are `ht0` and `ht1`. The Brownian term is the expected absolute increment, while the coefficient tail comes from a control-independent payoff bound. Both disappear as $t\uparrow1$, by integrability of $\gamma$. No derivative estimate at the cusp is required.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_uniform_deri: Every positive spatial derivative of the value is uniformly bounded on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$ for fixed $T<1$. Given `m`, the theorem controls derivative order $m+1$ by a finite constant independent of time and space within that strip. The assumptions are `hT0` and `hT1`. The constant may depend on the coefficient and cutoff; this statement alone does not provide uniformity over arbitrary families of coefficients.
notes.OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.zero_gap_curvature: If the coefficient is zero on $(a,b)$ with $0\le a<b<1$, the derivative of the curvature moment is strictly positive in the interval. The assumptions `ha`, `hab`, `hb` and `hc` give the domain and zero plateau. Equivalently, $q''>0$, so $q'$ strictly increases. This is a separate heat-case argument and does not divide by the coefficient. The statement covers only interior times, even when the interval begins at zero.
